## Eve Air Mobility
Type: operator | Status: announced | City: Dubai | Country: UAE | Last verified: 2026-08-22
Summary: Eve Air Mobility's UAE record: a 2022 Falcon Aviation letter of intent for up to 35 eVTOLs and a 2023 Kookiejar Urban ATM deal. No UAE operations to date.
Facts: Parent and listing: Eve Holding, Inc. (NYSE: EVEX), an Embraer company; Bahrain and other releases are carried on Embraer's official media centre. · Aircraft: The Eve 100, a lift-plus-cruise eVTOL with eight dedicated lift rotors and fixed wings for cruise. · Capacity and range: Four passengers plus a pilot at entry into service, with a stated range of 60 miles (100 km), per Eve's own aircraft page. · UAE commitment (2022): Letter of intent with Falcon Aviation Services for up to 35 eVTOL aircraft, announced 7 June 2022, aimed at tourist flights from Atlantis, The Palm. · UAE commitment (2023): Letter of intent with Kookiejar, announced 13 November 2023, for Eve's Vector Urban ATM software to support a proposed eight-pad vertiport hub with local partner Air Chateau at Al Maktoum Airport, Dubai South. · Order book: Approximately 2,700 aircraft under letters of intent and 100 aircraft under binding agreements with pre-delivery payments collected, as reported in FY2025 results on 16 March 2026. · Certification status: Type certificate application filed with Brazil's ANAC in February 2022; EASA type certificate validation application submitted in July 2026; six conforming prototypes targeted for flight test in 2027. No UAE regulator is named in Eve's certification releases.

## REGENT Craft, Inc.
Type: operator | Status: planned | City: Abu Dhabi | Country: UAE | Last verified: 2026-08-22
Coordinates: 24.4539, 54.3773
Summary: REGENT Craft plans Abu Dhabi seaglider manufacturing with the Strategic Development Fund. Seagliders are maritime wing-in-ground craft, not eVTOL aircraft.
Facts: Headquarters: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, United States · Craft: Viceroy seaglider — 12 passengers or roughly 1,600 kg of cargo, all-electric · Company-stated performance: Up to 180 mph (about 290 km/h) on routes up to 180 miles (about 290 km) per charge · Regulatory class: Maritime vessel — Type A wing-in-ground-effect craft, not an aircraft; US Coast Guard and Lloyd's Register, not the FAA or GCAA · UAE anchor partner: Strategic Development Fund, an EDGE Group company; investor since 2023, initial joint-venture agreement 26 February 2025 · UAE government engagement: Memoranda with the Abu Dhabi Investment Office and the Department of Municipalities and Transport, April 2024 · UAE service target: 2027 entry into service stated by the company and by SDF; no UAE sea trial has taken place

## VPorts
Type: operator | Status: announced | City: Dubai | Country: UAE | Last verified: 2026-08-22
Summary: VPorts signed a 2022 agreement with the UAE GCAA and Dubai South for a 37,000 sqm advanced air mobility integrator centre. No primary evidence it was built.
Facts: Dubai site: 37,000 sqm at Mohammed bin Rashid Aerospace Hub (MBRAH), Dubai South, under a 25-year exclusive lease renewable for a further 25 years · Agreement date: Announced 7-8 December 2022 by VPorts and Dubai Media Office · Named counterparties: UAE General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) and MBRAH / Dubai South; GCAA cited as allocating segregated airspace for flight testing · Announced investment: US$40 million initial investment over three years; lead investor named as NEXA Capital Partners · Announced timeline: Construction from 2023, operations and first flight testing from 2024 — no primary source confirms either occurred · Aircraft-developer agreements: Electra.aero, Falcon Aviation and SkyDrive announced 15 March 2023; Electra and SkyDrive confirm on their own newsrooms, Falcon does not · Second UAE site: A vertiport at Ras Al Khaimah International Airport announced 15 March 2023 with RAK Airport and RAK Department of Civil Aviation; no timeline given
